_what: The person's files files at the local door (src/account_files/account_routes.rs): at `resource`, each of `operations` is answered by the account files' tool of that name (src/account_files/mod.rs `call`, the hosted Worker's file contract: list_files {folder?, after?, limit?}, find_file / show_file {name_or_identity}, read_file {name_or_identity, offset?, length?, encoding?: auto, text when the bytes are UTF-8 and not an image, or base64, always base64}, files_summary {}, usage_days {after?, limit?} (the account's own usage day rows, src/account_files/usage.rs), write_file {name, text | content_base64, media_type?}; share_file {name_or_identity, seconds}, a URL that GETs the file without other credentials for 1 up to 604800 seconds, whole or by byte range (only host is signed, so a recipient streams it), as often as its holder likes until it expires, kept as an @namespace/shares record, never the URL) or one of its generic name operations (src/account_files/names.rs: find_names {prefix, after?, limit?}, the names in the prefix's folder that start with it; move_names and copy_names {from, to, after?, limit?}, a name or a whole folder of names, at most `limit` steps a call, answering next_after until done; set_aside and put_back {name, after?, limit?}, a name or folder moved into the set-aside tree at the same full name and back; list_set_aside {folder?, after?, limit?}). Only name records change: a file and its bytes are never copied or deleted by them. forget_set_aside {name, after?, limit?} forgets a set-aside name or folder for good and notes each file for the byte release; retire_names {names: [{name, expected_identity, retire: true}]} sets aside and forgets owned temporary names by exact path and expected identity, answering {retired, repeated, conflicts} (src/account_files/names.rs). The byte release (src/account_files/release.rs): queue_release {limit?} turns noted files nothing holds into release rows and forgets their records; release_gone_bytes {limit?} claims those rows, removes each object from its store and reports it released, until the call's time ends; list_released {after?, limit?} pages the storage given back. Results kept about files (src/account_files/results.rs), by content identity and kind and found by any of the file's identities: record_file_results {results: [{identity, kind, value, produced_by?, only_if_absent?}]}; read_file_results {identity, kind?, caller?}; read_file_result_fields {identity, kind, fields, caller?}; list_file_results {kind?, after?, limit?, caller?} (no kind: the count of each kind); read_file_results_many {kind, identities, caller?}; merge_file_result {identity, kind, value, produced_by?, only_if_empty?}; remove_file_result {identity, kind}. dav {prefix, method, path, depth?, range?} answers one request of the read-only WebDAV folder (src/account_files/dav.rs) as {status, headers, body_base64}, for the door's /dav route; dav_write {prefix, method: PUT | DELETE | MKCOL | COPY | MOVE | LOCK | UNLOCK, path, depth?, destination?, overwrite?, if_match?, if_none_match?, if?, lock_token?, timeout?, content_type?, body_base64?} answers one write of the same folder the same way (src/account_files/dav_write.rs: a DELETE sets aside, never forgets; a LOCK is an @namespace/dav-locks record); neither is ever a tool run's. A read past the caller's most open reads answers {busy, retry_after_seconds}. The account's files lives in its state folder in the file its resources are placed in (src/storage/record_store_resources.json, a record store the account files migration made); an account without one answers that its files is unavailable. Bytes are read and written through the account's origin records, signed by the account's secrets vault. `run_operations` are what a Workshop tool run may be granted here (invoke.records.rights[]: {files: "/" for every name, or a folder path ending in "/" for the names under it; operations}), each with its rule of what one call touches (account_rights/run_rules.rs): a call naming a name (`id`, each of them when it names two: a move's from and to) or a folder (`id_prefix`) is covered by a folder right when the name or folder is under it; a call naming a file by its identity, or the whole account files (files_summary), only by a right on every name. `run_outputs.folder` is where the files a finished Workshop run made are kept (src/tool_runs/tools/outputs.rs, for a row's invoke.outputs): `<folder>/<tool>/<run>/<file>`, written by the engine itself, so a tool needs no right here to have its output kept.

search._what: The words in the person's file names, searched with one question (src/account_files/mod.rs AccountFiles::search, the port of old trillion src/search.mjs:1364 `words-in-names`, the `file-names` lane of src/search.json). Input {question, limit?}: the question cut to `question_chars`, its distinct words of at least `min_word_length`; candidates are the files the record store word index holds (every text of a `@namespace/files` record is indexed at write time, its `names` among them) for every uncommon asked word (a word with `word_hits` postings narrows nothing), and a file is kept when every asked word starts a word of the last part of one of its names. Answers {question, terms, results: [{id, source, identity, name, path, title, media_type, byte_length, found_in, places, said, address: {resource, operation, input}, score}], unavailable, pending}; the score is `rank` over (`k` + the file's rank), the weight the old lane had, so a caller merges it with the records' answer (records-routes.json `search`) by rank: a Workshop tool does, as old trillion src/search.mjs:1750 `finish` did; the engine merges nothing. `limit` is 1..`most`.

_page: The person's own signed-in page reaches these same operations at its route (src/server/owner-routes.json, the row whose family is `resource`; AccountFilesDoor::page_call): GET /work/api/files/<operation>?input=<JSON> for each of `page.reads`, POST /work/api/files/<operation> with the input as its JSON body for every other operation. The page's session admits the call (src/local_workspace.rs call_files), and the call runs through `call_while`, the same call an AI's key makes at this door: the same operations, the same inputs, the same answers.
_old_paths: The paths old trillion's signed-in page called for the person's files (Trillion-X/trillion tag old-trillion-before-worker-retire: src/worker.mjs:824-827 handed every /work/api/namespace/* path to the account's Namespace owner; src/namespace.mjs:2107 handleNamespaceApi, src/namespace-results.mjs:465 handleResultsApi and src/work-media.mjs:88-94 /recent-files answered them), each answered by the one operation here that old src/file-tools.mjs:125-166 made of that same path: list_files called POST /namespace/listing {collection: folder, after, limit}, files_summary GET /namespace/summary, read_file POST /namespace/contents/read, find_file POST /namespace/files/lookup, the results tools /namespace/results*, write_file POST /namespace/write, recent_files and record_file_use /recent-files. Each row is that call read backwards (src/account_files/page_paths.rs): its method and path after /work/api ({name} one whole segment, percent-decoded; `unless` the exact paths another owner keeps), the operation, and each input field's source as the old route read it: body:<field>, body (the whole JSON body), query:<name> (its first value; :number a whole number above 0, else left out as old `Number(x) || default` left it to the default), path:<name>, a list (the first present) or {value}; `segments` holds the pattern a {name} segment must match where the old route refused another (GET /namespace/files/<x> and /namespace/contents/<x> answered 400 unless x was a content identity, so a file name never travels in a URL: old src/namespace.mjs:2304-2321; GET /namespace/results/<x> the same, old src/namespace-results.mjs:494). An absent source leaves the field out, so this door's refusal of a missing field is the answer. The page's session admits each call, as every page call here (AccountFilesDoor::page_call); the owner route that sends these paths to this door is src/server/owner-routes.json's row of this resource.
_call_bytes: What lets in the bytes a call here reads or writes (src/account_files/source_reads.rs): `counted` lets them in under one name and counts each byte as the account's own usage (usage.rs day rows, which the Workshop's take-payments rows read); `refused` lets none in, so every physical read and write refuses before a request is sent and only listing, finding and stat answer. `funded` lets in only what the host's funded allowance for the account covers (see _funded).
_funded: How a computer that funds bytes by holds opens each account's allowance, read only when call_bytes is `funded` (src/resource_authority/budget/account_files.rs Funded, opened by the host at start, src/native_entry.rs): the newest unrevoked, unexpired signed capture of unit namespace-file-bytes in the account's own protected funding home (@resource-budget/funding) funds an Allowance (src/account_files/source_reads.rs) of chunk_bytes holds, refilled below low_water_bytes off the request path. Only captures signed under signature_domain by one of `issuers` (public keys, base64url) are trusted; an empty list trusts none, so every byte of a funded door is refused until a real funding issuer's key is listed here.
_recent: The files the person used most recently and how (old trillion src/recent-files.mjs and src/recent-files.json, ported one to one onto account rows: src/account_files/recent.rs). A use is {file, kind}: `kind` matches `kind_pattern`, and `words` only says how a kind reads (a kind with no row reads as itself, first letter raised, dashes as spaces). The engine stamps the time. One row per file in `@account-files/recent/files` (id the file's identity) holding each kind's newest time, and one row per file in `@account-files/recent/order` whose id sorts newest first; at most `keep` files are kept, the one used longest ago leaving first. `uses` are the door operations that keep a use when they answer: a row's `operation` keeps `kind` for the file its input names (`file`, a name or identity), and `when_zero`, when set, keeps it only when that input field is absent or 0 (a read from the start, not every range after it). `recent_files {limit?, before?}` reads `list_default` (at most `list_max`) newest first, a renamed file by its name now, a file no longer kept left out; `record_file_use {file, kind}` keeps one use.
_facts: The facts kept about each file are its result of kind `kind` (old trillion src/file-tools.mjs:135 set_file_facts, the results merge of kind facts: POST /namespace/results/<identity>/merge {kind: 'facts', value: facts}). `set_file_facts {identity, facts, produced_by?}` is that merge (src/account_files/results.rs merge_file_result): only the facts it names change, null takes one away, the same facts again write nothing, and the facts are kept under whichever of the file's identities already holds them; it answers {identity, kept_under, kind, value, changed}. They are read back with read_file_results {identity, kind} like every other result, and bounded by `results.max_value_bytes`: one owner for every result, no second row.
_usage: The account's own usage counts (src/account_files/usage.rs): every flush_seconds the one flush thread adds each counted account's stored, read and worked counts to its day row in @namespace/usage, off every request path. usage_days {after?, limit?} reads those rows (a right on every name, as files_summary).
_setup_facts: Get started's facts about the account's own mechanics (Round 2 contract C): `operation` at `resource`, input {user_agent?, origin?} (the asking browser's, as old trillion GET /setup/facts?user_agent=&origin= took them; text, at most `most_input_chars` each), answered by src/native_boot/mcp_local.rs setup_facts_at, never by the files' own `call`. Ported from old trillion src/native-setup.mjs facts() (tag old-trillion-before-worker-retire, lines 196-271) and trillion-rust src/workspace_setup/facts.rs and src/local_account/setup_sign_in_inventory before 2159cb24. It answers {facts, signed_in, shared_rules, context}: `signed_in` {names, complete} the account's own sign-ins as old signedInAppNames gave them (its connected apps' registered names, then its keys' names, each once, apps first: setup_sign_in_inventory/projection.rs names), what old devicesFor read as `signedInAs`; `shared_rules` and `context` the operator's published show rules and setup context (the service records this computer keeps, src/local_account/service_records.rs; old readSetupPolicy's operator.workspaceRecord), null when none is published and left out when they cannot be read. `facts` holds only the facts whose owner is in the engine and answers them one to one, so a Workshop tool reads every fact left out as unknown (old setup-steps: a fact not sent is unknown, never done). Left out, and why: `owned` (the profile, pursuits, connections and records counts) and `access`/`freeDecisionAccess` (the plan) are features' records, read by the tool from records (engine-feature-boundary.json); `aiConnected`/`aiApps` need the person's AIs as they introduced themselves (old src/connected-ais.mjs: an `ai` record naming the sign-in it came in on), which no owner keeps today, so the tool joins `signed_in` with those records when they exist; `runtime` (the setup runtime), `notificationDevices`, `computers` (the computers' own reports), `devices` (it needs the device releases, old readDeviceDistribution) and `knownAt` (the last setup snapshot, old setup-known) have no owner in the engine since 2159cb24 removed them, so they stay unknown.
_held_connections: Which of the person's connected accounts hold values in the account's vault, by the names alone (the account mechanics a connections list needs and only the vault knows): `operation` at `resource`, input {}, answered by src/native_boot/mcp_local.rs held_connections_at, never by the files' own `call`. The vault (src/secrets.rs, the running tools job that holds a run's secrets) keeps a connection's values under the names src/tool_runs/tools.rs held_name gives them (`service-connection-<hex of the connection id>` and `service-connection-<hex of the connection id>-field-<hex of the field id>`, the service-connections work contract's secret.name_prefix); `held_connections` reads those names (secrets.rs names_only, no value is opened) and answers {connections: [{connection_id, fields}]}, each connection once in connection id order with the field ids it holds, sorted. A name of any other shape (a refresh's stored expiry, a pending rotation, another tool's secret) is not a connection's and is left out. No value, expiry or handle ever leaves. It is what the original held-values `list` stood on (src/held-values.mjs before 4ffa1dc4a2: the box's connections) for tool:list-connections (Workshop tools/connections), whose facts beside it (service, status, checks, who connected it) are the person's own `connection` records.
